subject_ref: multi-steward topology: queue + prod delivery under several stewards (brief 2e4a0d6403eb1cf7f947cd0c985e52e5d5ab0429b73b898341d48e7ea7618427)

claim: Recommend C+E: any branch steward enqueues into the one serialized queue (merge-queue.yml:66 concurrency group, merge_queue.py DEFAULT_BATCH=4); only prod bless/migrate/deploy keeps a single lease. Enqueue is a local rebase+gates+push of an mq/* ref with a CI-judged outcome, so gating it behind the release lease (release_steward.py, noc-steward SKILL section 1) adds a serial human hop with no safety gain; the real race (bless/promote/deploy, migration-before-image on one VPS) is what needs exclusivity. Splitting the lease into 'queue-submit' (open to any registered steward) and 'prod-release' (exclusive) removes failure 11 for the queue half.

Term overload: 'steward' means two roles, and the canon documents only one. release-steward.md:1 and noc-steward SKILL.md:6 define 'the steward' as THE one session that enqueues/blesses/deploys, while the brief's 'branch steward' appears in no KB pattern or CLAUDE.md (grep of PATTERNS/ and CLAUDE.md finds none). A newcomer reading 'ONE elected steward' would conclude the branch steward is illegitimate or must not exist, so the doc must define the branch-steward role (and give it another name) before any shape is chosen.

Split delivery (failure 1) is a queue-contract gap, not a steward-count issue: add an atomic delivery group id (BE+FE as one train entry via task_branch_train, or a group key the drain refuses to land partially) so a member ejection ejects the whole group. Without it more parallel enqueuers make this worse; this is the construction leg and must ship with a gate that refuses a group-tagged partial landing plus telemetry on group ejections, per gate-methodology-sync.

Authority boundary of the branch steward is unwritten and apparently contradicts the hook table. release-steward.md:106 makes enqueue/integrate/landed and pushes to mq/* steward-only, yet the brief says a branch steward 'delivers stage entries into the single queue'. An outsider cannot tell whether it files release_steward request (and who then enqueues) or enqueues directly; fresh sessions will guess, as failure 3 shows.

Do not build D/F (per-product lanes or per-product deploy leases) yet: deploys are serial on one VPS, seed/lib touches every suite, and merge_queue.py has no path-scoped suite selection, so lanes need new affected-product test selection and a cross-product coordination rule, with ejections costing ~1 CI cycle today and no measured contention. Measure first (queue wait time, ejection rate by cause, count of concurrent enqueuers) and revisit when queue wait exceeds a stated threshold; option B (one agent for everything) re-creates failure 11 and consent round-trips.

The recovery model for sessions depends on state a newcomer cannot find: the lease lives in ~/.noctus/release-steward.json (release-steward.md:26) outside the repo, and the role-to-session mapping does not exist (brief failure 3). After a reboot or a week away, the only way to learn who holds which role is a status call plus ListAgents with changed session names; the docs give no 'who am I / what role was I' entry point, and noc-steward SKILL.md is absent from the feature worktree, so a fresh branch session has no procedure at all.

Survivability: a lease with 7200s TTL (release_steward.py:81) plus pid liveness is slow to recover after reboot (failure 2) and handoffs by session name break on restart (failure 3). Add a role registry keyed by role (queue-submit, prod-releaser, branch-steward:<branch>) with auto-claim on session start when the lease is stale/dead-pid, an inbox reconciler that drops requests whose head_sha is already on dev (failure 4), and a TTL shortened with heartbeat from the Monitor. Prod consent stays typed in the releasing session by design; make the prod-releaser the same session that runs migrations so no relay is needed.

Jargon density blocks cold reading: bless, promote, landed, train, drain, batch_limit, mq-candidate, ejected, keeper, hw_admission, 'gated is not blocked' are used unglossed in the brief and noc-steward SKILL.md sections 3-6. The release path (bless then promote then deploy_image) is never stated as one ordered sequence with who is allowed to run each step in one place, so a newcomer would likely run the wrong tool or wait on the wrong session.

Branch stewards (shape E) should hand over via a single train/entry with a stated migration-number reservation and release parked-branch reservations on park (failure 5); the per-product migration collision gate is already correct at enqueue. Derived artifacts (failure 9) should be regenerated by the drain post-compose, not by enqueuers, so parallel entries stop coupling on KB counts/baselines/lockfiles.

The release lease is machine-local (~/.noctus/release-steward.json, release-steward.md:26; release_steward.py:13) while prod is ONE shared VPS and the queue is on GitHub. A second machine or a cloud session gets its own lease, so two 'sole' releasers can bless/migrate/deploy concurrently, which is exactly the race the steward was adopted to prevent. Six months out the lease must live on a shared substrate (e.g. a git ref or GitHub environment/lock keyed on prod), with role->session registry, not a local file.

The drain concurrency group 'merge-queue' (merge-queue.yml:66-68) is a single global lane with whole-queue batches and no path/product scoping. As stewards and products multiply, one ejection costs a full 13-25 min CI cycle for everyone, and seed/lib entries couple all suites. Design the queue now so batches can be partitioned by changed-path class (seed/lib vs per-product) and tagged with a train/atomic-group id, otherwise throughput degrades linearly with steward count and split delivery (failure 1) recurs.

Role handoff is by session name, which changes on restart (brief failure 3), and the lease is per-session not per-role. Adding stewards (branch, per-product, cloud) needs a durable role registry (role -> current session, resumable after reboot/TTL expiry) with auto-reclaim by the next fresh session, otherwise each new steward tier multiplies the manual re-assignment cost seen in failures 2 and 11.

Enqueue is inside the lease although the queue already serializes merges: the drain runs in one GH Actions concurrency group (brief, merge-queue facts) and enqueue does local rebase/migration-renumber/keepers on the caller's own branch (task_branch enqueue). The release-steward.md:11-19 rationale says 'N sessions could still race to enqueue', but enqueue pushes a unique mq/<slug>--<sha7> ref, so no shared resource is raced; gating it behind one lease is inherited habit that creates failure modes 2 and 11 (deliveries waiting on one session's availability).

Enqueue is lease-gated today (release-steward.md:25 lists enqueue among holder-only actions; hook table at :106 denies `--task-branch enqueue|integrate|landed` to non-holders), yet the queue itself is already serialized by one GitHub concurrency group (brief, merge-queue.md). So shape C is not what runs: enqueue sits behind the same lease as bless/deploy, and failures 2 and 11 (stale lease, consent round-trip) stall deliveries that need no prod authority. Cheapest increment: drop enqueue/landed from the lease hook (keep bless/promote/migrate/deploy), since the race it guards (dev collisions) is already removed by the queue; one hook-table edit plus a test.

The only operations that are inherently single-actor are bless, prod migrations and deploy_image: one VPS, serial deploys, and consent typed in the acting session (brief constraints). The lease (release-steward.md:11-19, release_steward.py DEFAULT_TTL_S=7200) should shrink to exactly that prod-touching set; the brief admits no race was ever measured on enqueue/landed, so widening it to the queue has no evidence behind it.

No role-to-session registry exists: handoff is by name (`handoff to_name=`, release-steward.md:58-60) and election is `ListAgents` guessing (:41-47), the exact mechanism that failed in failure 3 when names changed on restart. A branch steward tier (shape E) adds a second role with no lookup at all. Cheapest increment: a role file (e.g. `~/.noctus/roles.json` keyed by role + branch -> session_id, claude_pid, heartbeat) written by `claim`, which `request` and SendMessage resolve; `request` already works through the outbox so it needs no live peer.

Several observed failures are not steward-count problems at all, so adding or removing stewards fixes none of them: split delivery (1) is a missing atomic-entry rule (BE+FE must go as one train entry, task_branch_train); stale entries/inbox (4), parked migration number (5), merge-driver absolute paths (6), derived-artifact coupling (9) are hygiene/tooling defects. Fix those directly rather than choosing a topology to route around them.

Failures 2 and 3 (stale lease after reboot, handoffs naming sessions) share one root: identity is a session name/pid, not a role. A tiny role->current-session registry (or lease claimable by any session with automatic takeover on dead pid/boot id, rather than waiting out a 2h TTL) removes both without new topology; consent relay (10) stays by design, so keep the typed-consent step the only owner round-trip.

Split delivery (failure 1) is a bundle-atomicity gap, not a steward-count gap: `request` is per-slug (release-steward.md:62-65) and a BE+FE pair enters as 2 entries; the train action exists (brief) but nothing forces pairs through it. Cheapest increment: add a `bundle=<id>`/`requires=[slug]` field to `release_steward request` and have the drain-list step refuse to enqueue a member separately, routing the set through `task_branch train`; testable by filing one half and asserting it stays queued.

Recommended shape: C with enqueue unleased. Any branch steward or session enqueues/trains into the single serialized queue (no lease, idempotent, atomic multi-branch trains for coupled pairs); one lease-holding releaser does bless+migrate+deploy only, taking over automatically when its holder dies. Reject D and F: per-product lanes/leases need a cross-product rule for seed/lib changes that touch every suite, and the 8 GB Mac plus one VPS make the extra parallelism buy little since CI minutes are free and the real wait is the owner's consent.

Per-product lanes / per-product leases (shapes D, F) are the most expensive to build on the 8 GB Mac with a per-product migration gate and seed/lib changes hitting every suite: path-scoped suites need a seed/lib-touches-everything escape hatch that makes most batches global anyway, and prod is one VPS with serial deploys. No incident in the brief is a lane-throughput problem (all 11 are ownership/identity/derived-state). Recommend deferring D/F until a measured queue-wait metric exists; ship telemetry (queue wait per entry, lease idle time) first per gate-methodology-sync.

Shapes B and C protect the wrong layer: no deploy tool holds a resource lock (grep for flock/mutex in deploy_image.py, deploy_pull.py, migrate_product.py, release.py finds nothing), and the lease is a per-Mac file ~/.noctus/release-steward.json (release_steward.py:~175-215) that lets session-less callers through as 'unattributed' (release_steward.py:789-798). So 'one releaser' is advisory against a second machine, CI or raw ssh. The dismissed alternative is a short-held action mutex at the VPS/tool (deploy and migrate take it, migration-before-image ordering enforced inside it), so ANY session may ship and the steward stops being a person; that removes failures 2, 3, 4 and 11 instead of managing them.

Lease staleness is the only recovery path: TTL 7200 s with claude_pid liveness as the sole fast path (release-steward.md:81-83), yet failure 2 left nobody owning the queue after a reboot until the owner reassigned by hand. Nothing specifies what state a dead holder leaves mid-sequence (migration applied, image not swapped; spec 10 at :72-75). Cheapest increment: on claim over a stale lease, print the last in-flight step from release-steward.ndjson (migration applied? image pinned?) before proceeding.

Failures 10 and 11 show the true bottleneck is the owner's typed consent, not the lease: consent must be typed in the acting session, so an elected releaser that is not where the owner is typing forces a relay that is refused by design. The unconsidered shape is 'the shipper is whichever session the owner is currently typing in, holding a short action lock', rather than an elected long-lived holder; B and C would keep failure 10 at 100 percent of prod migrations.

Shape E (branch tier / train) trades split delivery for blast radius: a train enters the queue as ONE entry and the queue ejects only at entry granularity (merge-queue.md:281, 'a red singleton is ejected'), so one environment-dependent test, the exact cause of failure 1, ejects the whole branch at about 25 min per retry, and the cost grows with branch size. A long-lived integration branch also concentrates the derived-artifact coupling of failure 9. The cheaper fix for failure 1 is a declared `requires`/`ship_with` ordering between two small entries (FE entry held until BE lands, or both composed in the same batch), not bigger entries.

Shape D (per-product lanes with path-scoped suites) would have missed failure 8 (contract path plus component-name clash) and failure 9 by construction, since path scoping is file-disjointness and file-disjoint is not effect-disjoint. Seed/lib changes hit every suite, so lanes degenerate to one lane plus a coordination rule that does not exist yet.

The 11 observed failures contain no bless/promote/deploy race; all are state-registry or handoff failures (stale lease, session names, stale inbox, parked migration number, merge-driver paths). The 2h stall after a reboot is concrete: liveness falls back to heartbeat TTL when pid is unknown (release_steward.py:~112, DEFAULT_TTL_S=7200 at :81). Any shape change before shipping a role-to-session registry, pid-based and boot-aware lease reclaim, inbox reconciliation against landed state, and migration-number expiry for parked branches will inherit all 11 failures; the shape choice matters less than these.

Shape C, not B: dev is already serialized by the GitHub concurrency group (.github/workflows/merge-queue.yml:66-68) and the drain composes/bisects/ejects on its own (merge_queue.py:537-601), so the machine lease adds no safety to enqueue/landed - it only adds the single-owner wait of failure 11. Open enqueue+landed to every steward; keep the lease solely for the irreversible, shared-VPS, consent-bound steps (bless, promote, prod migrations, deploy_image). Reject A for those steps: deploys are serial on one VPS and consent must be typed in the acting session, so one prod releaser is the correct one-way-door owner.

There is no atomic co-landing unit: a queue Entry is exactly one mq/ ref (merge_queue.py:133-140), so a BE+FE contract pair filed as two entries can be split by ejection (failure 1) and dev then holds an undeployable half. Construction: a delivery that touches a contract-first pair must enter as ONE entry (train by default, task_branch train), with an enqueue-time gate that refuses a ref whose declared partner slice is still open, plus telemetry counting split landings.

Lease liveness cannot survive a reboot: _pid_alive returns True for an unknown pid and a recycled pid after reboot reads as alive (release_steward.py:110-114, 247-250), and a stale lease is only replaced when some session explicitly claims (release_steward.py:297), which is failure 2. Key liveness on boot-id + heartbeat, auto-offer takeover at every session start, and make handoff address the ROLE (role->current-holder registry in the lease file) instead of a session name, which closes failure 3 by construction.

The steward inbox is a hand-synced second ledger (ship-requests.ndjson) beside the queue's own truth (mq/ refs + commit statuses, merge_queue.py:378-386), so it drifts (failure 4). Derive request state from the queue (queued/landed/ejected by sha) on read instead of storing it; 'derive, don't sync by hand' is already a section-1 rule.

Reject per-product lanes (D) and per-product leases (F) for now: seed/lib, CLAUDE.md, migration chains and derived artifacts couple every product's suite (failures 7-9), so lanes would need a cross-lane coordinator that recreates the single queue with more failure surface. It is a two-way door - record queue-wait p95 and ejection-cause telemetry per entry and revisit only if wait time, not red batches, measures as the dominant delivery cost.

Migration numbers are reserved too early: a parked branch held a number that blocked another session's enqueue (failure 5) because number allocation counts every local branch, while the drain already rejects true duplicates against dev+queue (merge_queue.py:152-169). Allocate/renumber only against dev + entries already in the queue at enqueue time, so a parked branch never holds a slot and renumbers itself when it is enqueued.

decision: RECOMMENDATION (council informs; stewards decide): shape C + slim E. (a) one serialized merge queue, enqueue/landed open to any session/integration-branch owner without lease; (b) prod (bless/promote/prod migrations/deploy_image) exclusive via a short-held shared action lock, eventually held by the session where the owner typed consent; (c) integration-branch owners deliver small entries tied by atomic delivery groups, not large trains. Defer per-product lanes/leases until telemetry shows queue wait dominates.
biggest_risk: Loosening the lease before a shared prod action lock exists: two sessions/machines could bless/migrate/deploy the one VPS concurrently (lease is local to one Mac, unattributed callers pass). Secondary: atomic groups coarsen ejection.
first_step: Fix lease liveness in release_steward.py (boot-id + pid + heartbeat; unknown pid not alive; stale-claim shows last in-flight step), with test + telemetry.

dispositions.reason: no lock in deploy/migrate/release tools; unattributed pass-through release_steward.py:787-799; build item 11 owner-gated
unknown pid counted alive release_steward.py:105-114, TTL 7200 :81; build item 1 first
drop enqueue/landed from lease hook; build item 10, owner-gated
blocker; verified Entry is a single mq/ ref (merge_queue.py:133-140); atomic delivery groups = build item 8
path-class batch partitioning deferred to build item 13, triggered by queue-wait telemetry (item 3); atomic group-id half accepted under TK

note: noctusai-22 adopts recommendation (narrowing: atomic groups opt-in for declared contract pairs); line 22 relabelled S->A after concurrent-write race (pre-repair copy kept); contrarian claims leaked to tech-lead pre-verdict via error path, disclosed. b5 decision pending.
